inspiration.observed_pattern: A grouped CTE filters entities with HAVING SUM(...) and an UPDATE JOIN consumes the qualifying entity IDs to apply a status mutation.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a membership-spend refresh. Because MariaDB 10.11.7 rejects the source's WITH-before-UPDATE form, the grouped qualifying relation is expressed as a derived table; HAVING keeps accounts above a spend threshold, and an UPDATE JOIN marks only those accounts as priority. The source schema, names, values, and user-order context are not copied.

fixture_notes: Accounts 11 and 12 exceed the settled-spend threshold and are updated; account 13 reaches exactly the threshold, account 14 has only a cancelled invoice, and neither changes. Existing account notes remain unchanged.
determinism_notes: Account IDs, invoice IDs, states, amounts, derived-table grouping, HAVING threshold, assignments, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE membership_accounts (account_id INT PRIMARY KEY, account_label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, account_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, status_note VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE membership_invoices (invoice_id INT PRIMARY KEY, account_id INT NOT NULL, invoice_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, amount_cents INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: UPDATE membership_accounts AS a JOIN (SELECT account_id FROM membership_invoices WHERE invoice_state = 'settled' GROUP BY account_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 10000) AS q ON q.account_id = a.account_id SET a.account_state = 'priority', a.status_note = 'spend-threshold'
SELECT account_id, account_label, account_state, status_note FROM membership_accounts ORDER BY account_id

checks.sql: SELECT account_id, account_label, account_state, status_note FROM membership_accounts ORDER BY account_id
